extracted.intended_audience: scientometric researchers, publication-ethics scholars, journal editors and policy makers
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical bibliometric/scientometric analysis of retracted publications (Iran-affiliated) including identification, classification of retraction reasons, descriptive statistics (time-lag, journals, institutions), collaboration metrics, and visualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: COPE situations warranting retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: COPE suggests that journal editors should consider whether or not to retract an article in one of the following four situations: (i) the editors have an evidence that the findings are unreliable, either as a result of misconduct or honest error; (ii) the same findings have already been published and this fact was not properly addressed (e.g., by obtaining permission or providing a reference); (iii) the article plagiarises another published document; or (iv) the article is based upon unethical research (Wager et al., 2009).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use COPE's four-condition test as a standard for deciding on retraction. Examples and related labels (honest errors, misrepresentation, data manipulation, poor data management, plagiarism including self-plagiarism, duplication of text, failure to disclose conflicts of interest) can be mapped to these situations when classifying retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible grounds / example reasons for retraction (COPE examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on COPE and Wager et al. (2009): 'honest errors,' 'misrepresentation', 'data manipulation,' 'poor data management' (such as the author being unable to generate data to support his or her results), 'plagiarism' (including self-plagiarism), 'duplication of text,' or 'failure to disclose conflicts of interest'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coding reasons for retraction, consider this list as canonical dispositions to map free-text retraction notices to standardized reason categories; treat self-plagiarism as distinct from plagiarism where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad cause taxonomy for retractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Causes behind retractions are generally divided into three categories: research misconduct, scientific errors, and moral and/or political reasons (Aspura et al., 2018; Wager and Williams, 2011).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify individual retraction reasons under these three high-level buckets for comparative analyses across studies and countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search/inclusion strategy for retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: Query Scopus with the search term 'retract*' and an additional country filter to choose Iran-affiliated retraction notices for a specified time window (here: 2001–2019). Manually check retrieved records to filter out non-retractions (titles containing 'retract*' but not actually retraction notices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated database queries must be followed by manual inspection to remove false positives; export results as CSV for reproducible downstream analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and merging of multiple data sources (Scopus + Retraction Watch)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain reasons and broader context, merge Scopus-derived retraction notices with the Retraction Watch database; use Retraction Watch when it provides more complete reason metadata and to compute share of Iranian retractions in global retractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer combining bibliographic databases with curated retraction databases for richer coding of reasons. Retain only matched records for analyses that require reasons; use broader databases when estimating country shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review and COPE-based categorization with consensus resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction reasons retrieved were independently reviewed by researchers and categorized based on COPE guidelines; inconsistencies were resolved by discussion and final agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement independent dual coding (or more) and consensus meetings to improve reliability of categorical assignment; document decision rules for ambiguous or multi-reason notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction reason categories used in this study (eleven categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors categorized retraction reasons into eleven categories: fake peer review, plagiarism, duplicate publication, authorship problems, scientific error, publisher error, falsification/fabrication, copyright claims, conflict of interest, unspecified, and other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this 11-category scheme (or map to it) when coding retraction reasons to allow comparability with this study; allow multiple reason tags per paper (see 'multiple reasons' guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fake peer review (reason category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fake peer review — counted as a distinct retraction reason (95 cases in the sample); often associated with higher Modified Collaboration Coefficient (MCC), indicating multi-author involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag fake peer review separately; expect it to appear often in journal articles and to sometimes co-occur with other reasons (e.g., authorship problems). In analyses, report counts, share, and mean publication-to-retraction time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism (reason category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism (including self-plagiarism) — a primary reason for retraction (90 cases in the sample).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat plagiarism as both standalone and co-occurring reason; note that plagiarism/self-plagiarism tends to be associated with lower MCC (more often fewer authors) than reasons like fake peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate publication (reason category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplicate publication — retraction reason for a subset of papers (64 cases); observed to have the longest average P-R (publication-to-retraction) time in this sample (about 3,000 days in some instances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coding duplicate publication, differentiate from acceptable republication practices and document whether duplication was text-only or results; expect long detection lags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship problems (reason category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorship problems — a retraction category (32 cases); associated with higher MCC values (tendency toward multi-author papers in the sample).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code disputes over authorship, ghost/guest authorship, manipulated authorship or author-order issues distinctly; consider institution-level patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific error (reason category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific error — retraction due to honest or unintentional errors in data, analysis or conclusions (31 cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish honest scientific errors from misconduct; where possible record whether authors requested the retraction (author-initiated) and report P-R times separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher error (reason category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher error — papers retracted due to publisher-side mistakes (e.g., duplication by publisher) (23 cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish errors introduced by publishers (e.g., production errors, duplicate posting) from author misconduct; these cases affect interpretation of 'retraction as indicator of misconduct'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Falsification/fabrication (reason category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Falsification/fabrication — intentional data manipulation or invention of data (7 cases in this sample).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as severe misconduct; report separately and consider downstream effects (citations, societal harm).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright claims (reason category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright claims — retractions issued due to copyright infringement claims (4 cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code legal/rights-based reasons separately from scientific or ethical misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest (reason category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict of interest — retractions due to undisclosed conflicts (2 cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag undisclosed COIs as distinct governance failures; small counts may still be important qualitatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unspecified (reason category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unspecified — retraction notices that do not provide a reason (84 cases in the matched sample); many of the unspecified cases were conference papers with very short P-R times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat unspecified notices as a separate category; recognize that they impede quantitative analysis of causes and require qualitative follow-up or exclusion for cause-specific studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other (reason category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other — catch-all category used when the stated reason did not fit standard categories (23 cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples or subcoding where feasible; avoid overuse of 'other' as it reduces interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple reasons per paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Some retracted papers were assigned more than one reason; in the study reasons sum to more than 100% (433 reasons for 343 papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow multi-label coding for retraction reasons; when reporting shares, indicate whether denominators are papers or reason-instances and clarify that totals may exceed 100%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication-to-retraction time-lag (P-R) metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure P-R as the number of days between publication date and retraction date; used to compute average/mean P-R per reason and overall (overall mean reported as 591 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report mean and distribution of P-R; compare P-R across reason categories (e.g., duplicate publication often long P-R, unspecified often short, conference papers short). Use P-R to discuss detection and editorial reaction times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified Collaboration Coefficient (MCC) as collaboration metric
rubrics_metrics.description: MCC (Savanur & Srikanth, 2010) computed as: MCC = 1 - (sum_j f_j / (n * k)) * ((A - n) / (A - 1)) [paper provides formula], where f_j is number of papers with j co-authors, n total papers, k largest number of authors, A total number of authors. MCC ranges between 0 and 1; close to 0 indicates single-author trend, close to 1 indicates multi-author trend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MCC to quantify degree of multi-authorship in a set; compare MCC across reason categories (authors observed higher MCC for fake peer review and authorship problems).

rubrics_metrics.name: MCC interpretation limitation for small sets
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors noted they did not determine MCC for sets with fewer than 10 papers, since MCC has limited interpretation in such instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not compute or interpret MCC for very small samples (n < 10); report this threshold and justify any deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document/source-type classification and erratum labeling caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify retractions by source/document type (e.g., journals vs conference proceedings). Scopus sometimes classifies retraction notices as 'errata' even when that term isn't used in the notices themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify database document-type labels against the original retraction notice text; treat conference proceedings differently (many had unspecified reasons and short P-R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution-level normalization metric (RP/TD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalize institutional retraction counts by calculating the share of retracted papers to total documents from the institution (RP/TD) — used to avoid misleading conclusions from raw counts (e.g., Islamic Azad University had many retractions in raw counts but a small RP/TD share).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always report both raw counts and normalized shares (RP/TD) when comparing institutions; highlight institutions with unusually high RP/TD even if raw counts are small.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization/collaboration-network inclusion threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: When visualizing the international collaboration network, include only countries that shared at least three retracted publications with Iranian authors for readability (full set contained 27 countries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply and report explicit inclusion thresholds for network visualization to balance comprehensiveness and readability; indicate that thresholds affect observed network composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of data-source differences and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize limitations of data sources: different databases (Scopus vs Retraction Watch) provide inconsistent coverage (e.g., Retraction Watch contained 728 Iranian retractions vs 343 in Scopus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple data sources when possible, report coverage differences transparently, and restrict analyses accordingly (e.g., use matched records when reasons are required; use larger database for country-share trends).

rubrics_metrics.name: Software/tools and reproducible workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Data extraction and analysis were performed using Excel 2016 and IBM-SPSS version 24.0; international collaboration map visualized with VOSviewer; data exported as CSV for analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and version-control data extraction queries and code; provide CSV exports and specify software versions to enhance reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding practice for transparency and qualitative follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors note that unspecified reasons and inability to identify responsible authors limit quantitative studies and recommend qualitative follow-up (editor and author interviews) for deeper understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When many notices are unspecified or responsibility is unclear, plan qualitative studies, interviews, or case-level investigations to complement quantitative coding; document limitations in interpretation.
